transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-09-11
Time: 09:00 PT / 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~58 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Park (Redwood AE), Maya Singh (Redwood SE), Carlos Ruiz (Redwood CSM); Dana Lowe, Ravi Menon, Priya Shah, Leah Kim (Avelon)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be fuzzy):
- Focus: quarterly health check on usage, cost burn, and upcoming roadmap alignment for Avelon inference workloads.
- Key blockers: VPC routing limits, unexpected tail latency on long-context workflows, cost surge in experimentation buckets.
- Agreed next steps: Redwood to provide trimmed pricing scenario for a 3-month pilot and run a focused tail-latency benchmark on the Dedicated pool with the customer's trace. Security deep-dive to follow.

Topics:
- usage trends and burn profile
- latency SLOs and tail behavior
- Dedicated vs Hosted tradeoffs for compliance windows
- roadmap features: prefix caching, autoscale/burst, quantization suggestions

Transcript body:
[00:00] Jordan Park: Okay uh good morning good afternoon everyone thanks for joining the Avelon quarterly sync. I think we have an hour so we'll try to cover usage, burn, and then walk through roadmap alignment stuff. Maya's going to jump into the perf numbers.

[00:22] Maya Singh: Hi all, thanks. quick caveat my slides are in the deck link in the chat. I ran the end-to-end 95 and 99 latencies last night, used their sample traffic from last month, and also tried a long-context path (about 2K tokens). Results — the Dedicated pool with burst enabled hit 95th at ~180ms and 99th at ~420ms for the short context. Long context tails were noisy, 99th up to 1.6s. These numbers are roughly consistent with what we saw in June but there's been an uptick in the experimentation namespace which increases prefix cache churn.

[01:10] Dana Lowe: 1.6 seconds on the 99th for the long contexts, is that with KV cache on? we thought we had prefix caching configured.

[01:20] Maya Singh: Yes, it was with prefix caching enabled but the workload has a lot of varied prefixes and the KV cash — cash in transcript — yep, kv cash churn is high, so cache hit rate is low for those calls. We can tune the cache TTL and also suggest smarter batching windows.

[01:45] Ravi Menon: Quick question on the Dedicated vs hosted math — our security team is clear they'd prefer private for PHI experiments, but finance is worried about the committed spend. How do you recommend we balance the latency guarantees vs the cost hit?

[02:05] Jordan Park: Good question. Short answer, Dedicated gives you predictable headroom and better tail control because you control the GPU pool sizing and kernel choices. Hosted is cheaper on trials and for spiky workloads if you accept a broader latency distribution. For PHI we usually steer customers to Private or Dedicated plus VPC peering for auditability and KMS integration.

[02:38] Leah Kim: on the finance side we saw last month a 48% increase in non-prod inference spend; that's largely from the model-sandbox project. Is there a way to throttle or cap that so we don't blow the pilot budget?

[02:55] Carlos Ruiz: We can add per-namespace quotas and rate-limits, and also suggest a cost-saving plan: quantized model variants for sandbox and batching to reduce token unit cost. Also there's an optimize report we can run to give exact tail savings per config. I'll put that in the follow-up.

[03:18] Priya Shah: Also on network, we hit some V-P-C route limits when we attempted cross-region calls; that caused request retry storms and spiked our token usage. Is that something Redwood's side can help debug or is that strictly on our infra?

[03:36] Maya Singh: We can help instrument the retries — we have tracing hooks you can turn on that show request routing and fallback policy. Often it's a combination: the customer's LB retries plus our routing fallback to other regions. We'll need packet-level traces from your infra to fully diagnose but we can isolate which path is triggering reroutes.

[04:02] Dana Lowe: Security question: we need SOC two evidence and SAML SSO integration, K-M-S key wrapping, and audit logs for every token request. Do you have those artifacts or is that separate engagement?

[04:20] Jordan Park: We have SOC 2 Type II cert and a security pack; Maya will schedule a security deep dive. For SAML we support SAML 2.0 with SCIM provisioning; KMS integration supports customer-managed keys for Private and Dedicated via our KMS bridge. Audit logs are available with optional extended retention add-on. We'll share the security doc link after the call.

[04:55] Ravi Menon: If we do dedicated with KMS and VPC, what's the timeline to get it running in production? We're aiming for mid-November for full rollout.

[05:10] Maya Singh: Typical lead for Dedicated w/ VPC + customer KMS is 6–8 weeks once we have access for network setup and your infra team completes the peering checklist. If you want mid-November we should start the provision/runbook in late-September.

[05:35] Dana Lowe: ok that fits. Another item: we had a quality regression on the latest quantized model — 2% BLEU drop on one eval set. Are you able to advise? We can't accept that in prod.

[05:50] Maya Singh: Yep, we saw similar in some workloads — quantization often shifts distributions. We recommend mixed precision for critical paths or using a calibration subset to tune the quant profile. Our Optimize team can run a quick eval/rollback plan.

[06:12] Leah Kim: back to cost — Jordan, can you present a trimmed pilot pricing that includes an option: dedicated small commit + burst credits vs hosted unlimited but throttled? We want a clear cost floor and an overage behavior.

[06:28] Jordan Park: Absolutely, I'll share a three-scenario model: hosted scaling, small Dedicated commit with burst credits, and a Private pilot option. I'll include predicted monthly spend and a worst-case tail assumption.

[06:44] Priya Shah: For the benchmark you ran, can you re-run with our production trace for 9/02? that will help show expected 99th and cost per token.

[06:55] Maya Singh: yes please send the trace, ideally scrubbed for PHI; we can run the 9/02 trace with both hosted and dedicated configs and capture p95/p99 plus cost delta.

[07:10] Ravi Menon: Competitor check — we did a POC with Anthropic briefly; their tail seemed better in small batch tests but cost was higher. Any notes on when Redwood would prefer one kernel path vs another?

[07:25] Maya Singh: We pick kernels based on sequence length distribution and model arch; for long contexts we use attention kernels optimized for streaming. There's also a quant-friendly kernel path for reduced memory and lower cost which can trade a slight perf delta. We'll include the kernel selection notes in the benchmark report.

[07:50] Carlos Ruiz: Quick ops note: I'd like to propose weekly short syncs for the next three weeks while we run the pilot tests. That keeps things moving and reduces alignment lag.

[08:03] Dana Lowe: that works. Also can you add an agenda item for the security deep-dive and the billing cadence?

[08:12] Jordan Park: yes we'll include security + billing in that first follow-up.

[08:20] (small crosstalk) Speaker 1: uh, sorry, can you repeat the SAML scoping doc link, I didn't catch it?

[08:30] Jordan Park: link will be in the follow-up email, and Carlos will attach the pilot template.

Recap and close:
[08:45] Jordan Park: Recap: Maya runs targeted benchmark on your 2025-09-02 trace. Jordan shares three-scenario pilot pricing spreadsheet. Carlos runs Optimize report and proposes namespace quotas and throttles. Schedule security deep-dive and a weekly 30-min pilot check-in starting 2025-09-22.

[09:10] Dana Lowe: Sounds good, thanks everyone.

End of transcript.
